messages.content: Plan the move of the reading group into a hall that is already booked for Wednesday. I need the sequence, not a mood.

Confirm the hold is Wednesday, check the deposit refunds until noon the day before, name a person who is actually in town that morning to pick up the key, and only then tell the group which room is the backup if the lights fail.

Confirm Wednesday's hold, check that the deposit refunds until noon the day before, name who picks up the key, then tell the group the backup room. 'Book the hall' was already done, so it isn't a step.
Sequence a two-week kitchen job. We still cook every night. Deliveries only when someone is home at 3pm.

<think>

The sink has to stay until the new one is in the room, and the room only receives deliveries at 3pm, so the new sink cannot be assumed in the morning. The night the sink actually comes out needs a meal that doesn't use it, named in advance.
The first pass optimized the contractor's start. The second pass optimizes dinner, which was the constraint.
Order that survives: deliveries at 3, unused cabinets first, sink last and only on a camp-stove night.

Take deliveries at 3pm. Demo the run you aren't cooking on. Leave the sink until the new one is in the room, and pull it on a night you already planned to cook on a camp stove.
